title: Derrick Strait: OU's 2003 Nagurski and Thorpe Winner
question: Which Oklahoma cornerback won the Nagurski Trophy and Thorpe Award in 2003?
answer: Cornerback Derrick Strait won both the 2003 Bronko Nagurski Trophy and the 2003 Jim Thorpe Award. He was the second OU defensive back in three seasons to win the Nagurski, after Roy Williams in 2001.
summary: Derrick Strait swept the 2003 Nagurski Trophy and Thorpe Award at OU, setting school records for pass breakups, career starts and interception return yards.
body: Two years after Roy Williams swept the top defensive honors, Oklahoma did it again. In 2003 senior cornerback Derrick Strait won the Bronko Nagurski Trophy as the nation's best defensive player and the Jim Thorpe Award as its best defensive back. He was the second OU defensive back in three seasons to win the Nagurski and the third Sooner to win the Thorpe, after Rickey Dixon and Williams.

Strait, a 5-foot-11, 195-pounder from Austin, Texas, made 80 tackles in 2003, third-most on a 12-2 team, and intercepted three passes for 127 return yards. His best day came in the 65-13 rout of Texas on Oct. 11, when he made 11 tackles, broke up three passes, recovered two fumbles and grabbed an early interception. Against Texas Tech on Nov. 22, he returned an interception 97 yards.

He was remarkably durable and productive over four years. Strait started at cornerback all four seasons, beginning with the 2000 national championship team, and left OU holding career records for passes broken up, career starts and interception return yards. OU's career totals credit him with 14 interceptions for 397 return yards and 52 pass breakups.

Strait was a unanimous All-American in 2003 and a two-time first-team All-Big 12 pick. The New York Jets drafted him in the third round in 2004, and he later returned to Norman as a graduate assistant on Bob Stoops' staff in 2012.
